metric_rationale: The experimental design explicitly pits Take The Best against Tallying on every single trial. Since the validities are strictly descending in feature index, TTB will always choose the option that wins on the first discriminating feature from left to right. Tallying will always choose the opposite option because the design ensures the other option has a higher total number of positive cues. By computing the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the TTB prediction, we will get a value close to 1.0 for data simulated under TTB, and a value close to 0.0 for data simulated under Tallying.

This metric isolates trials where Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) make diametrically opposed predictions. By computing the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic on these specific trials, we expect Tallying-simulated data to yield a value significantly greater than 0.5, whereas TTB-simulated data will yield a value significantly less than 0.5. With half of the experimental trials designed to be opposing, the metric ensures a highly stable estimate per subject.
